criteria.c5: cancel_appointment: PERMANENTLY cancels an existing appointment as soon as it is called — only call after the user explicitly confirms. The outcome is awaited, so a failed request is reported as a failure and nothing is changed. Cancellation is not reversible.
criteria.c6: __finish__: The task is complete. Report an answer supported by the observations.
criteria.c7: __abstain__: Stop because the task cannot be completed with the available actions or evidence.

criteria.c1: list_services: Read-only: list every bookable service with id, duration, price, location, description and the providers who offer it. Use the returned service id (and provider id) with check_availability and book_appointment.
criteria.c2: sign_in: Sign in to the back office with a username and password. The back-office tools (list_customers) are not registered until this succeeds, so call it first when the task needs staff-side data; then re-list the tools to see what became available.
criteria.c3: check_availability: Read-only: fetch the real open appointment slots for a service on one or more days (same source as the visible calendar). Times are in the business-local time zone, 24h "HH:mm", and are directly bookable via book_appointment. The visible wizard calendar is updated to the queried service/provider/date so the user sees the same slots.
criteria.c4: book_appointment: CREATES a real appointment at this business as soon as it is called — do not call until the user has confirmed service, time and contact details. Requires an open slot from check_availability ("date" + business-local "time"). On success the visible wizard reflects the selection, the page navigates to the booking confirmation screen, and the response includes the appointment id plus the personal manage/cancel link (which the site also emails to the customer when email notifications are enabled). If the slot was just taken, the response lists the remaining open slots.
criteria.c5: cancel_appointment: PERMANENTLY cancels an existing appointment as soon as it is called — only call after the user explicitly confirms. Requires the appointment_reference token from the customer's confirmation email (the site's own manage-link key); it cannot be guessed or looked up by email address. The appointment is first verified; if it exists and is still cancellable it is cancelled and the site's own cancellation confirmation screen is shown. The outcome is awaited, so a failed request is reported as a failure and nothing is changed. Cancellation is not reversible.
criteria.c6: __finish__: The task is complete. Report an answer supported by the observations.
criteria.c7: __abstain__: Stop because the task cannot be completed with the available actions or evidence.

actions.description: Look up this school's own content to answer a visitor question. Read-only retrieval across the school's profile (name, about, contact links) and the full course catalog: titles, descriptions, learning outcomes, tags, instructors and syllabus outlines (chapters and lesson titles). Returns matching content sections with their page paths — compose the answer from them. Use for questions like "do you have a beginner Python course?", "what does the SQL course cover?" or "who runs this school?". Returns empty matches when the site has nothing on the topic.

query.description: Natural-language question or keywords to look up

actions.description: Search this school's published course catalog. Read-only. Filter with a free-text query (matches titles, descriptions, outcomes and tags); with no query it lists the whole catalog. Returns structured matches — name, course_id, description, tags, instructors, page path — and navigates the page to the catalog results so the user sees the same list. Returns an empty list when nothing matches.

query.description: Free-text search terms (optional)

actions.description: Get full detail for one this school course: description, learning outcomes, instructors and the complete syllabus (chapters with lesson titles), plus the signed-in learner's enrollment status. Read-only. Pass course as a name or a course_id from search_courses; the page navigates to that course so the user sees it.

Enroll in a this school course (free enrollment). Enrolling requires a signed-in account: while signed out this tool does NOT enroll — it opens the sign-in page and returns guidance. After the user signs in, call it again to complete the real enrollment. Pass course as a name or course_id from search_courses.

Sign in to this school with an email and password. Do this first for anything tied to an account — enrolling in a course, or reading your progress — because those tools only exist once signed in. Browsing and course questions do not need it. After signing in, re-list the tools to see what became available.
